scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being unreasonable in this situation with my dad. Let me start by understanding what happened. I took my dad's business idea, which he came up with but never acted on, and I ran with it. I got the IP rights, started the business, and it's been a massive success. Now, my dad is upset, feeling betrayed, and even called me a "fucking asshole." I offered him 20% of the profits, but he rejected it and told me to get out. First, I need to think about the dynamics between me and my dad. He's more introverted and quiet, and while he's intelligent, he lacks the ability to get things done. On the other hand, I'm more impulsive and headstrong, but I get things done. I took his idea because I saw its potential, and I believed in it more than he did. I thought by acting on it, I was doing the right thing, especially since he hadn't done anything with it. But now, he's hurt and upset. He feels betrayed because I took his idea without his consent. I can see why he feels that way. Ideas are personal, and when someone takes your idea and runs with it, especially if it's successful, it can feel like a betrayal. I offered him a share of the profits, which shows that I value his contribution, but he rejected it. Maybe he feels that the offer wasn't enough, or perhaps he's hurt that I didn't consult him first. I also need to consider the bigger picture. My mom and granddad support me, which is good, but my sister is defending my dad. This family conflict is adding more stress to the situation. I need to think about how to resolve this in a way that respects both my dad's feelings and my own actions. Maybe I should have talked to him before taking the idea. Even though he didn't act on it, it was still his idea, and taking it without discussing it could have been seen as disrespectful. On the other hand, I believed in the idea and thought I was doing the right thing by making it a reality. I also need to consider the legal aspect. I got the IP rights, which means I legally own the idea now. But legally owning it doesn't necessarily mean I'm in the right morally. Morality and legality can sometimes be separate issues. Perhaps I should have found a way to involve him in the business, even if it meant sharing control or profits. That way, he would feel like he's part of the success, which might have lessened his feelings of betrayal. I also need to think about how to mend the relationship. Family relationships are important, and while I stand by my actions, I also need to acknowledge his feelings and find a way to move forward together. In the end, I think I did what I believed was right, but I can see why he feels wronged. Maybe the best approach is to continue to offer support and find a way to reconcile our differences, even if it means making some compromises.
